confirmed.requirement: collaboration-startup-handoff.md:47-48 says a legal 64 KiB assignment must stay whole ("Keep the admitted delegation whole"). design.md:70,72 says the admitted delegation is never silently trimmed and that a maximum-size legal multibyte delegation can still start.
confirmed.summary: handoffSource redacts the delegation before it applies the 64 KiB cap. redact.Text replacements are often longer than the text they match, so a legal delegation near 64 KiB that contains credential-like text comes out as truncated=true. The daemon refuses any truncated delegation, so that member run can never launch.
confirmed.failure_scenario: A leader posts a 65,000-byte @member comment. That is under CollaborationCommentMaxBytes = 64<<10, and comments are not redacted on write. The comment includes about 60 config lines like `TOKEN=x` (7 bytes, replaced by "[REDACTED CREDENTIAL]", 21 bytes). The redacted body grows to about 65,840 bytes, above 65,536, so content is cut and Truncated=true. The snapshot is stored, and every restore recomputes the same truncation (snapshot.go:107-111). validateHostHandoff then finds no `available && !Truncated` delegation and returns ErrProtocol, which retryHandoff does not retry. Every claim of this member run stops before launch, and the admitted step is never executed.
confirmed.evidence: collaboration_runtime_handoff.go:117-121: `content := redact.Text(body); truncated := len(content) > maxBytes`. Line 175 calls handoffSource("delegation", ..., body, 64<<10). collaboration_mentions.go:119/122 limits raw content to 64<<10, and CreateRuntimeComment (collaboration_squad.go:213) only sanitizes. redact.go:69,72,75 contains expanding replacements such as "Bearer [REDACTED]", "[REDACTED CONNECTION STRING]@" and "[REDACTED CREDENTIAL]" for `(?i)...TOKEN\s*[=:]\s*\S+`. host_handoff.go:108-115 accepts a member only when `source.Availability == "available" && !source.Truncated`, otherwise `return ErrProtocol`.
confirmed.verifier_reason: I confirmed the defect from the code. handoffSource (server/internal/service/collaboration_runtime_handoff.go:117-125) runs redact.Text(body) first and only then compares len(content) > maxBytes, with maxBytes = 64<<10 for the delegation (line 175). Raw content is only checked against CollaborationCommentMaxBytes = 64<<10 (collaboration_mentions.go:119-122). Neither the runtime comment handler, CreateRuntimeComment (collaboration_squad.go:213, which only calls SanitizeTextForPostgres), nor the CLI redacts on write, so a delegation that is legal at the cap can grow past 64 KiB once redacted. The generic credential rule in server/pkg/redact/redact.go matches `TOKEN=x` (7 bytes) and replaces it with "[REDACTED CREDENTIAL]" (21 bytes). A Python reproduction of that regex (no lookarounds, so RE2 behaves the same) turns a 65,000-byte body with 60 `TOKEN=x` lines into 65,840 bytes, so truncated=true. No later step repairs this. boundCollaborationHandoff (collaboration_runtime_handoff.go:454-491) never changes delegation sources. restoreStoredHandoff (collaboration_handoff_snapshot.go:107-111) recomputes the same truncation with the same limit. The daemon's snapshot request ID is deterministic (uuid.NewSHA1 of the run ID), so every claim gets the same envelope. validateHostHandoff (host_handoff.go:108-116) accepts a member only when `available && !Truncated`, so it returns ErrProtocol. retryHandoff does not retry a validation failure, and host_runner.go:185-188 stops before launch. The requirement does mandate the opposite. collaboration-startup-handoff.md:47-48 says "Keep the admitted delegation whole", and design.md:70,72 says the delegation is never silently trimmed and that a maximum-size legal multibyte delegation can still start. The spec allows redacted content (line 53-54) but not a truncated assignment. The finding does not match any KNOWN ITEM. The existing test TestCollaborationHandoffSnapshotPreservesMaximumAssignment (collaboration_runtime_handoff_budget_test.go:15-63) pads a 64 KiB assignment with '<', '&', '\x01' and '中', none of which match a redaction pattern, so it does not cover this case. The scope is narrower than the claim implies. Only host-mode member runs (HandoffVersion 1) are affected, because the non-host DispatchComment path returns the raw body. The trigger also needs a delegation near the 64 KiB cap that contains short credential-like matches. Even so, the failure is deterministic and permanent for that admitted step, and it breaks an explicit design guarantee, so medium stays.

confirmed.verifier_reason: I confirmed the defect from the code; none of the five refutation checks succeeds. (1) Every continuation reports completeness "unknown". buildCollaborationHandoff sets "unknown" by default (collaboration_runtime_handoff.go:159), and projectHandoffCauses only changes it to "recorded" when the run is not a continuation (collaboration_handoff_wakeup.go:101-105). Nothing distinguishes legacy runs from new ones. One builder serves the frozen snapshot (collaboration_handoff_snapshot.go:52), the runtime live read (:139) and the human read (:149), so the leader prompt and the panel both get "unknown". (2) No guard makes "unknown" true for new continuations. Every continuation is created by queueContinuation (collaboration_squad.go:348-367; CreateCollaborationDerivedRun has no other caller). Each caller records its cause in the same group-locked transaction. Runtime comments record at squad.go:288, joined inputs at squad_join.go:119, and member proofs record pending at capabilities.go:746, then drain at squad.go:436-440. The pending query (collaboration_handoff.sql:30-35) loops until nothing is left unassigned. After a claim, the continuation stops matching the queued-continuation query, so later causes go to the next run. A continuation created after this feature therefore holds the complete cause set. (3) The design asks for more than this. design.md:66 says wakeup_causes holds every source actually assigned, and only incomplete old records get marked. prd.md:67 (R5) and research/handoff.md:76 limit the marking to legacy runs with no retained causes. Marking every continuation "unknown" under-claims; it does not fabricate anything, but it goes beyond what was asked. (4) The finding matches none of KNOWN ITEMS 1-4. Item 2 covers recording/checkpoint text, not wakeup completeness, and design.md lists no accepted boundary for this. (5) No test pins either behavior for a real continuation. assertWakeupBoundaryCauses (collaboration_wakeup_boundary_test.go:253-268) and the merged-sources test (collaboration_runtime_handoff_test.go:128-132) check items, total and order but never Completeness. The only "recorded" fixture is synthetic (runtime_handoff_budget_test.go:69), and the frontend tests only feed "unknown". Severity stays low. The error is fail-safe: it hides information but grants no authority and invents no history. The model prompt still receives the items in full (host_runner.go:587), so the visible harm is the human panel. run-handoff.tsx:30 replaces the recorded count with "Earlier reasons were not recorded." / "早期续作原因未记录。" (en collaboration.json:738, zh-Hans :737). confirmed.summary: After one non-definitive checkpoint failure, the in-run sender stops uploading for the rest of the run. Every later chunk is written to the ledger but never sent, so the whole backlog depends on a single post-run replay window of at most 1 s. The server permanently refuses any chunk not committed before Stop or before the outcome commit.
confirmed.failure_scenario: A host run produces 13 chunks over 10 minutes. The first checkpoint POST hits the 1 s request timeout or a 503 collaboration_busy, which sets s.failed. Chunks 2-13 are staged locally and never POSTed. (a) If the user presses Stop at minute 8, recoverHost replays chunk 1 and gets 409 execution_stopped (collaboration_runtime.go:353-355). The daemon marks it Rejected, marks every later chunk Rejected, and seals with reason authority_lost. The server keeps 0 messages, although a working sender would have committed about 12 chunks before Stop. (b) Even on normal completion, recoverHostRecording gets at most 1 s. Then the outcome is POSTed unconditionally. Once it commits, readCollaborationRecording sets state.outcome and every remaining chunk gets a definitive 409 checkpoint_out_of_order. Chunks that were not replayed in that 1 s are lost permanently, although authority never lapsed.
confirmed.evidence: host_checkpoints.go:139-141 `if s.failed.Load() { return }` runs right after stageHostCheckpoint. host_checkpoints.go:153-155 sets `s.failed.Store(true)` for any non-definitive error, and nothing resets it. The only in-run send is :143, with a 1 s timeout at :142. client.go:297-300 makes a single attempt with no retry. recordingDefinitiveRejection (host_checkpoints.go:181-184) classifies 408/429/5xx/transport as non-definitive, so they become sticky. host_runner.go:520-531 runs recoverHostRecording under hostRecordingRecoveryContext (<=1 s, host_checkpoints.go:186-194, plus its own 1 s cap at :202) and then always POSTs the outcome. collaboration_checkpoints.go:206-207 rejects `state.seal != nil || state.outcome` with 409. host_checkpoints.go:224-232 together with host_checkpoint_ledger.go:190-194 turn that 409 into Rejected, reject all later chunks and set Reason=authority_lost. TestHostCheckpointLocalFailureCannotRebaseQueuedMessages/uncertain_prefix_valid_suffix covers only 3 chunks against an instant fake server with no Stop, so it never exercises this loss.
confirmed.verifier_reason: I confirmed the defect by reading the code. In host_checkpoints.go, `failed` is set at lines 82, 121, 135, 150 and 154, and nothing ever clears it. After the first non-definitive error (408, 429, 5xx or transport, as classified at line 183), every later flush() stages its chunk (line 129) and then returns at line 139 without sending it. No retry of the oldest pending chunk happens during the run. The only replay is post-run recoverHostRecording, which has a 1 s budget for the whole backlog (lines 186-194 and 202). The server refuses whatever that replay cannot commit in time. After Stop, lockRuntimeBusiness calls currentAdmission, which returns 409 execution_stopped (collaboration_runtime.go:337-356). Once the outcome has committed, any later checkpoint gets 409 checkpoint_out_of_order (collaboration_checkpoints.go:206-207). Both 409s are definitive, so acknowledgeHostCheckpoint marks the chunk Rejected and sets Reason=authority_lost (host_checkpoint_ledger.go:190-193), and every later chunk is cascaded to Rejected (host_checkpoints.go:217-221). This is not a known item: items 1-4 cover CLI reads, envelope text, knowledge defects and design boundaries. It is also not an accepted boundary. Design.md:37 and parent R2 accept losing content that was never uploaded only after authority is lost. They do not accept the daemon giving up on uploads while authority is still valid. The follow-up-no-gap result.md assumes that a staged chunk stays recoverable. That assumption fails for the Stop path in parent AC4, because the server refuses uncommitted content after Stop. The trigger is plausible. Each request has a 1 s timeout, and the server's own NOWAIT retry loop gives up and returns 503 collaboration_busy after three lock conflicts (collaboration_runtime.go:446-477). I rate it medium rather than high. Nothing is falsely claimed complete: the outcome is marked partial (host_recording.go:237) and the seal reason shows the gap. The final outcome and proof paths still succeed, and there is no authority or security impact. The loss is limited to process-recording retention, but it is permanent, and on normal completion the seal mislabels the cause as authority_lost.

confirmed.summary: Each staged chunk keeps the business token and attempt_seq of the launch that was current when it was staged. After a fresh-session fallback is authorized, the server accepts only the newest attempt's capability. Any chunk from the earlier attempt that is not yet committed can never be stored. Its rejection closes the run-wide stream, so the fallback launch's recording is dropped too.

Replaying chunk K with its original attempt-1 token then gets 403 business_capability_required from lockRuntimeBusiness, or 409 stale_execution. The daemon treats that as definitive. Chunk K and every later chunk, including all of attempt 2's messages, are Rejected and the stream closes. The seal says authority_lost on a run whose authority was never withdrawn.

confirmed.verifier_reason: I confirmed the defect from the code, and none of the five checks refutes it. (1) The cited code behaves as the auditor claims. Each staged chunk carries the attempt seq/nonce of the last authorized launch and the BusinessToken that was current at staging time (host_checkpoints.go:117-129). The ledger persists that token (host_checkpoint_ledger.go:170). After the fallback, authorizeHost replaces Host.BusinessToken (host_ledger.go:284), and the server issues attempt N+1 with a new capability and bumps authorized_attempt_seq (collaboration_host_runtime.go:157-200; the AuthorizeCollaborationHostAttempt SQL). When an attempt-1 chunk the server never committed is replayed, it passes the capability-hash, cap.AttemptSeq==seq and validateRecordingAttempt checks, because attempt 1 is still nonce-matching and authorized_at-valid. It then fails lockRuntimeBusiness (collaboration_squad.go:93: capability.AttemptSeq != r.run.AuthorizedAttemptSeq) with 403 business_capability_required. Only an already-committed chunk avoids this, through the idempotent branch at collaboration_checkpoints.go:171-178. The daemon treats 403 as definitive (recordingDefinitiveRejection). acknowledgeHostCheckpoint then marks the chunk Rejected and sets Closed with Reason="authority_lost" (host_checkpoint_ledger.go:190-194). recoverHostRecording rejects every later chunk locally, including attempt-2 chunks that carry valid tokens (host_checkpoints.go:205-233). If the rejection happens in the live sender, closed is set and host_recording.go:64-66 drops all later messages. (2) Both trigger paths are reachable, and no guard prevents them. The sticky path: any transport error or 5xx sets s.failed (host_checkpoints.go:154), after which chunks are only staged, never sent, until recoverHost. recoverHostRecording is called only from recoverHost at the end of the run (host_runner.go:521), after the fallback at host_runner.go:224-245 has already authorized attempt 2. The race path: a tick flush stages a chunk under the attempt-1 token while authorize() has released the supervisor lock during the permit HTTP call (host_runner.go:312-317); the permit commits first and the checkpoint gets 403. requestHostPermit, authorize, bindHandoff and authorizeKnowledge never check hostRecordingChunksPending, and nothing flushes or awaits the sender before the fallback. recording_version is negotiated in production (handler/collaboration_runtime.go:197). (3) The requirement supports the finding: the spec says "The recording stream and offsets are run-wide across Provider retries" (collaboration-host-execution.md:104-105), and design.md:37 says a network-uncertain chunk whose original payload is still in the ledger is not counted as lost and is retried under the same identity. The run's authority was never withdrawn; a newer attempt only superseded it, yet the seal reports authority_lost. No task doc or spec records this as an accepted boundary. (4) It does not duplicate a KNOWN ITEM: those cover CLI handoff reads and paging, envelope recording text, knowledge-audit defects, and documented boundaries. (5) No test covers it. TestHostHandoffCheckpointFailureCleanup/fallback_snapshot_drift refuses the fallback (it asserts permits==1), so attempt 2 never exists. Its fake checkpoint server also accepts any issued attempt's token (host_handoff_checkpoint_test.go:70-72) instead of enforcing current-attempt-only as the real server does. Severity stays medium. The outcome and proof are still stored correctly, but a resume-rejected run with a single transient checkpoint error, or an unlucky tick, loses the uncommitted attempt-1 chunk and the entire fallback transcript, and its recording is sealed with a misleading authority_lost reason.

confirmed.requirement: design.md:41 seal 仅含 "枚举原因"; prd.md R1 "接手方可见最后确认保存的位置和缺失/裁剪原因"; parent AC4 (接收方可看到缺失范围)
confirmed.summary: The seal reason the daemon reports does not match the real cause. Every definitive 4xx is stored as authority_lost. The protocol value "stopped" is never produced. transport_error is effectively unreachable because a partial outcome always overrides it with incomplete. The receiver therefore cannot tell user Stop, revocation, transport failure, local validation failure and a superseded attempt apart.
confirmed.failure_scenario: A user Stop with a pending chunk is sealed as authority_lost because 409 execution_stopped counts as definitive. A stream closed by the REC-1 post-outcome 409 checkpoint_out_of_order on a normally completed run is also labeled authority_lost. A run whose upload simply failed is labeled incomplete, not transport_error. RunHandoff and records expose these reasons through retention.reason.
confirmed.evidence: host_checkpoint_ledger.go:190-194 sets `rec.Reason = "authority_lost"` for any rejected ack. recordingDefinitiveRejection (host_checkpoints.go:181-184) treats all 4xx except 408/429 as definitive. The only reasons ever produced are host_checkpoints.go:74 (recording_limit, also used for a local staging validation failure), :76, :256, :258 and :261/:268 (incomplete overrides transport_error whenever outcome.Record.Completeness==partial, which any non-definitive failure forces via host_recording.go:237). The server copies the reason at collaboration_checkpoints.go:105-108, and it is exposed via collaboration_runtime_handoff.go:254-255 and collaboration_records.go:267.
confirmed.verifier_reason: I confirmed the core claim from the code. The daemon never emits "stopped". It records every definitive 4xx checkpoint rejection, including a user Stop's 409 execution_stopped, as "authority_lost". "transport_error" cannot be reached. A local staging failure is reported as "recording_limit". The protocol enum (collaboration_checkpoint.go:92) and the server's own seal fixtures, which hand-write Reason "stopped" for Stop/revoke, both expect these causes to stay distinct. That makes R1's "缺失/裁剪原因" (the missing/trimmed reason) less precise than the design intends. This is not a KNOWN ITEM: item 2 covers what the startup envelope contains, not how seal reasons are labeled. No design.md boundary covers it either, because design.md:41 only says "枚举原因" (an enumerated reason) and never defines the mapping. No existing test asserts the daemon's reason for a Stop or revoke. One sub-scenario is overstated. A normally completed run that hits the post-outcome 409 checkpoint_out_of_order in a single recovery round is not labeled authority_lost. recoverHost (host_runner.go:476-521) stages the seal in its deferred call during the first round. With rec.Reason still empty and the outcome partial, the seal is persisted as "incomplete". ValidateCollaborationRecordingSealAdvance (collaboration_checkpoint.go:150) then forbids changing the reason, so a later rejected replay cannot relabel it. authority_lost appears only if the daemon crashes between the outcome ACK and seal staging. Severity stays low for three reasons. retained_through and observed_through, the actual missing range that AC4 requires, remain correct. The shared UI (packages/views/collaboration/run-records.tsx:93-97) shows only the retained and observed counts, never the reason. The reason reaches only the REST JSON of the records endpoint and GET /handoff, and per KNOWN ITEM 1 no CLI reads GET /handoff.

refuted.summary: The new outcome producer still folds result.Error into the same `body` field as model output, and the protocol has no discriminator for it. The handoff therefore shows a backend or daemon error string as an ordinary `provider_result` source, indistinguishable from real model output.
refuted.reason: The code does what the auditor says, but the design allows it. design.md:86 is a conditional rule: the new producer may mark a result final_answer only when a backend contract explicitly provides one, and "otherwise it stays provider_result/unknown". No backend has such a contract, and the protocol validator only permits final_answer_state unknown or absent. So every outcome body, including one taken from result.Error, correctly falls back to provider_result/unknown. The failure is still visible: the result item carries outcome=failure, progress and proof_state, and hostPromptWithHandoff marshals the whole envelope into the model prompt. The task PRD's background table names "outcome.body may come from a provider error message" as a known fact, and its stated gap is only that such results must not all be labeled the model's final answer. The research recommended kind=provider_result|squad_activity plus outcome, with no separate error kind. Tests and the acceptance addendum accept provider_result with unknown final-answer state for both success and failure outcomes. A leader seeing provider_result together with outcome=failure therefore gets the contracted signals: the run failed, the text is data and not a final answer. Adding an origin field would be new scope beyond the design.

refuted.summary: No code path ever produces availability=missing/purged while keeping the original hash. Replaying a frozen snapshot whose memory was purged returns a bare 409 handoff_source_unavailable with no envelope. A missing handoff, delegation or result source returns a raw error. The live projection's purged branch clears memory.sha256. The protocol and Core accept "missing"/"purged", but the server never sends them.
refuted.reason: The finding misstates the code and leans on one line of design.md that later, more specific contracts overrule. (1) The server does produce "purged". buildCollaborationHandoff sets Memory.Availability="purged" and appends missing "memory_purged" (collaboration_runtime_handoff.go:231-235), so the claim that the server never sends it is false. That path is the live current-read projection, not a frozen replay, so design.md:76's "keep the original hash on replay" does not cover it. (2) Half of the failure scenario is not a defect. design.md:81 requires the binding step to recheck "current readability, frozen revision/hash and purge state" and states that a failure blocks the launch. BindRuntimeHandoff returning 409 is therefore the mandated behavior, and the daemon test host_handoff_launch_test.go:340 ("purged", 409 handoff_source_unavailable → no start, not_started proof) pins it. (3) For snapshot replay, the authoritative contracts call for refusal, not a degraded envelope. collaboration-startup-handoff.md §4 says "Source purged/revoked … Stop the fallback; no fresh snapshot substitution" and "a replayed snapshot must equal the original". collaboration-host-execution.md:96-99 says that with handoff_version=1, re-reading a purged base means "startup/fallback is refused". The design research the line came from (research/handoff.md:45) explicitly allows "surface the loss or refuse supported replay rather than silently substitute". PRD AC4 asks only that a purged source does not leak through the snapshot, and the refusal satisfies that. (4) The only consumer of a snapshot replay is the daemon (host_handoff.go:64), and the result is the same either way. validateHostHandoff (host_handoff.go:95) rejects any non-"available" memory when a base is present, so an envelope with availability="purged" and the original hash would still be refused. No human or reader path consumes stored snapshots. RunHandoff and RuntimeHandoff build live projections. The 409 carries an explicit purge-class code (handoff_source_unavailable), so the claimed loss of the purged marker is not real. (5) The "missing" value for sources has no reachable purge trigger. Handoff notes (issue_handoff) and run events (outcome/comment/squad_activity) have no purge or delete query besides whole-issue or workspace deletion, which removes the run too. A raw error for a vanished ledger row is consistent with invalidCollaborationLedger handling, not a missing purge marker. At most, design.md:76's wording is looser than the spec, which is a documentation inconsistency with no behavioral or security impact.
